body_markdown:
Finding the right support isn’t always straightforward. As policies, eligibility requirements, and available services change, navigating the social safety net can become even more challenging for individuals and families seeking assistance.


At One Degree, we believe that access to reliable information is essential. But sometimes, knowing that a resource exists isn’t enough. People also want to know what to expect when they reach out, whether a service was helpful, and what others experienced along the way.


That’s where community voices make a difference.


## ****Learning from those who’ve been there****


Through One Degree, members can share their experiences with the services they’ve accessed, offering practical insights that help others navigate their options.


Over the past year, members across California and New York have shared feedback about everything from utility assistance and emergency housing to senior meals and residential care.


In San Francisco, a member who received help applying for discounts on[gas and electric bills](https://www.1degree.org/opp/get-help-applying-for-discounts-on-energy-bills) shared:


> “ *Was very helpful and good! I would tell my friends about the resources.* “


In Oakland, another member described an[emergency housing and meal](https://www.1degree.org/opp/get-emergency-housing-meals-and-east-oakland-community-project-oakland-ca) program as:


> *“very nice and useful 👍🏾”*


In Glendale, a member shared a helpful detail about a[senior meal program](https://www.1degree.org/opp/get-low-cost-lunch-for-seniors-city-of-glendale-glendale-ca) :


> *“This is the best tasting sit-down senior lunch anywhere in the LA Area. It’s free and served 7 days a week at 11:30 AM.”*


And in Long Beach, a member staying at a[residential care facility](https://www.1degree.org/opp/join-a-residential-facility-for-bixby-knolls-towers) described what made their experience feel welcoming:


> *“Sweet and humorous staff who are always willing to tend to my concerns. They feel like family here.”*


These experiences offer something that traditional resource listings can’t always capture: a firsthand perspective on what accessing support actually looks and feels like.


## **Why community experiences matter**


When people are navigating unfamiliar services, especially amid changing policies and requirements, hearing from someone who has already been through the process can make a meaningful difference.


In conversations with One Degree members, we’ve heard that reviews make unfamiliar services feel more approachable and help people decide where to invest their limited time and energy. Some members rely on firsthand experiences to determine whether an organization delivers the support it promises, while others use them to avoid pursuing services that may not meet their needs.


These insights also help One Degree improve the quality of our resource information. When members report that a service has changed its hours, moved, or is no longer available, that feedback can prompt our team to verify and update the listing.


## **Building a more informed, connected community**


As the social safety net continues to evolve, accurate information and community knowledge are both essential.


By combining verified resources with real experiences from the people who use them, we’re working to make it easier for individuals and families to find support they can trust.


To every One Degree member who has shared their experience: **thank you. Your voice is helping someone else take the next step toward getting the support they need.**
